title: Yara and the Hollow
premise: Bram Oyelaran, a hedge-witch mercenary whose god fell silent seven years ago, survives in the city of Vell by selling charms too small to register—until the crown's new Inquisition begins burning anyone who carries even a spark of the gift. Hunted alongside Yara, an orphan girl whose magic is dangerously loud, Bram flees into the Hollow, the drowned quarter beneath the city where the last dragon-fire still smolders. There she learns her silent god did not die: it was devoured by the thing wearing the king's crown, which feeds on bound divinity and has been hollowing the realm for decades. To save Yara and herself, Bram must unbind the king from his parasite at the cost of her own remaining power, choosing in the end not to restore her god but to let magic pass into ordinary hands—Yara's among them—and finally belong somewhere rather than hide everywhere.
about_author: Ulyana Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about faith, survival, and the people history forgets to burn.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the market city of Vell, Bram sells luck-knots and fever-charms, hiding her gift behind mundane craft while mourning her silent god, the Shepherd. A routine sale goes wrong when a customer's charm flares visibly. Emotional beat: weary vigilance—the cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Criers announce the King's Edict: all gifted persons must surrender for 'cleansing,' informers rewarded. Bram watches neighbors she's charmed for years look at each other differently. She burns her stock that night. Emotional beat: dread as community curdles into suspicion.

chapters.title: A Loud Little Fire
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara, eleven, orphaned and living in a chimney flue, cannot stop her magic from leaking—warmth, small lights, singing kettles. An Inquisitor's hound catches her scent; she barely escapes through the rooftops. Emotional beat: fierce, frightened resilience.

chapters.title: The Hound at the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Inquisition raids Bram's street following the flare from chapter one. Her old comrade-in-arms, Sergeant Doss, tips her off seconds before the door breaks. She escapes through the sewers carrying nothing but her god's broken prayer-bead. Emotional beat: betrayal and narrow escape.

chapters.title: What the Sewers Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Bram collides with fleeing Yara in the undercity; the girl's wild magic saves them both from a drainage flood. Uneasy alliance forms—Bram knows the old tunnels from her mercenary days. Emotional beat: reluctant trust born of necessity.

chapters.title: Down to the Hollow
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They descend into the Hollow, the drowned pre-city beneath Vell, where refugees of past purges survive around a guttering vein of dragon-fire. Its keeper, the ancient half-blind woman Sef, recognizes Bram's prayer-bead. Emotional beat: awe and grief—a hidden world of the discarded.

chapters.title: Sef's Ledger of the Burned
chapters.summary: Sef's POV (framed as told to Bram). Sef reveals the Hollow's history: every purge feeds the fire's opposite—a cold thing beneath the palace that eats bound gods. The Shepherd wasn't silent; it was swallowed. Emotional beat: revelation reframing seven years of abandonment.

chapters.title: The King's Cold Court
chapters.summary: Inquisitor-General Maren Voss's POV. At court, we see the king: vacant-eyed, perfect, repeating edicts in a voice not quite his own. Voss suspects the truth but serves anyway, believing order requires the thing on the throne. Emotional beat: chilling complicity.

chapters.title: Training the Storm
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram teaches Yara to cage her magic using mercenary discipline tricks; Yara chafes, wanting power, not control. Their bond deepens into something like family. First successful containment—but Yara asks why Bram won't use her own gift. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by avoidance.

chapters.title: Raid on the Hollow
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. Voss's hounds find a leak in the refugee network; the Hollow is raided. Sef dies holding the tunnel so others escape, the dragon-fire dimming as its keepers fall. Bram and Yara flee deeper with a handful of survivors. Emotional beat: devastating loss and guilt.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sheltering in a submerged chapel, Bram finds murals depicting the Shepherd's devouring—and her own face among the god's old sworn mercenaries. The binding that silenced her god runs through her bloodline. Emotional beat: horror at discovering she was always part of the design.

chapters.title: Voss's Doubt
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Auditing purge records, Voss finds the numbers don't balance: the gifted burned far exceed any census. She confronts the king privately and watches his shadow move independently. Shaken, she begins quietly falsifying reports. Emotional beat: a true believer cracking.

chapters.title: The Price of the Deep Road
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. To reach the palace foundations, survivors must cross the Deep Road, bartered passage with the river-thing Kessil, who demands a memory as toll. Yara secretly pays with her memory of her mother's face. Emotional beat: sacrifice foreshadowing the book's theme—what survival costs.

chapters.title: Under the Throne
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Beneath the palace they find the Crown's root: a hollowed god-corpse threaded through the foundations, still faintly whispering prayers—including the Shepherd's voice. Bram realizes unbinding the king means giving the parasite a new door: herself. Emotional beat: terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Doss's Choice
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Ordered to seal the undercity, Doss finds Bram's trail and must choose between his oath and the woman he once fought beside. He opens the gate and is caught doing it. Emotional beat: honor redeemed at personal ruin.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. With Sef's stolen notes and the dragon-fire ember carried from the Hollow, Bram begins the rite to sever king from crown. It requires a sworn vessel to hold what pours out. Yara refuses to let Bram do it alone. Emotional beat: love weaponized against fate.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Climax, multi-POV. The rite tears open; the parasite offers Bram her god back, whole, if she kneels. Tempted to reclaim seven lost years, she instead speaks the unbinding, and the thing floods toward her—until Yara's loud, uncaged magic gives it nowhere to hold. Voss turns her Inquisitors against their own master. Emotional beat: renunciation as triumph.

chapters.title: Ash and Ember
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The king wakes, human and ruined, remembering decades lost. The parasite, unanchored, gutters out against the dragon-fire ember. Bram survives but empty—her gift gone with the rite, her god truly dead now. Emotional beat: hollow victory, honest grief.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Vell
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. The Edict collapses; Voss publicly testifies, dismantling the Inquisition she built. Doss, imprisoned, is freed by the people he once policed. The city reckons with its years of denunciation. Emotional beat: uncomfortable, necessary accountability.

chapters.title: Yara's Hands
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The dispersed divine sparks settle into ordinary folk—and most strongly into Yara, who must decide whether to hoard power or teach it. She chooses teaching, opening the first honest school of the gift in Vell's rebuilt market. Emotional beat: belonging chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Prayer Without Answer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram, powerless, tends the rekindled dragon-fire in the restored Hollow alongside the survivors. She prays out of habit, then stops—not bitter, just finished. Doss stays; the city above slowly changes. Emotional beat: quiet peace after long exile.

chapters.title: The Last Light Carried Up
chapters.summary: Dual POV, closing. Yara brings the first class of students down to see the fire; Bram teaches them what she learned the hard way—that power kept is power corrupted, power shared is power survived. Above, bells ring for no god, only for the city. Emotional beat: hopeful resolution—belonging earned, not granted.
